rows.evidence: Q1: Methods, Performance and Error Analysis, Application sections - the authors run their own 1D Richards-equation and HYDRUS-2D axisymmetric simulations (220 and 156 runs) to generate training/test data and train/test a self-organizing map ANN.
rows.notes: The study develops and tests a SOM neural network that, trained on numerical flow-model output, returns the water application time needed to reach a desired wetted depth/radius for a given initial soil moisture (Figs. 5, 8). It demonstrates only that the SOM reproduces the flow model's results (MSE vs. test data, deviation about +/-1 cm); the ANN output is never compared with measurements from a real irrigated system, no water-use or water-saving is quantified, and the only link to measured data is Meshkat et al.'s (1999) prior lysimeter validation of HYDRUS-2D, which is cited, not the authors' own. The result is a precondition (a tool for determining application timing) for the claimed water-conservation effect, not evidence of it.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods, Performance and Error Analysis, Application sections - own numerical flow-model runs and SOM neural network training/testing.
rows.notes: No crop, yield or crop-production variable appears anywhere in the study; it only shows that a SOM can emulate a subsurface flow model and invert it to give irrigation duration for a target wetted soil volume (a 'crop-specific soil moisture profile' is only mentioned as the target). The ANN output is validated against model output, not real-system measurements. The study supports at most a precondition (determining timing) of the claimed yield effect.

notes: Full text appears complete (pages 287-297). The paper is a methodological/numerical study: physically based flow models (1D Richards equation; HYDRUS-2D axisymmetric with Meshkat et al. 1999 parameters) generate synthetic data to train a self-organizing map that predicts wetted depth from initial moisture and time, and inversely the application time for a desired wetted volume. No field or laboratory measurements of its own, no water-use or yield outcomes; the Fig. 6 check is model-to-model agreement with Meshkat et al. (1999).
